items.q: Match the following source iodine entries — 1) Adult requirement 2) Pregnancy requirement 3) Daily urinary repletion entry … A) >100 µg B) 220 µg/day C) 150 µg/day
items.exp: The source prints adult 150 µg/day, pregnancy 220 µg/day and daily urinary iodine >100 µg. Do not confuse this daily amount with population urinary iodine concentrations in µg/L. (Book p901)

items.q: A nuclear-medicine note concerns thyroid radioablation for Graves disease. Which isotope is paired with that use on the page?
items.exp: The source assigns I-131 to radioablation and I-125 to brachytherapy; these therapy notes should not be confused with all diagnostic scintigraphy protocols. (Book p901)

items.q: Assess the isotope note: I I-125 is paired with Graves radioablation. II Brachytherapy is a diagnostic thyroid-uptake scan.
items.exp: Brachytherapy is localized radiation treatment, not a thyroid-uptake scan; the source heading groups unlike applications. (Book p901)

items.q: The principal enzyme family responsible for peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion is the ___.
items.exp: Deiodination activates T4 to T3 or inactivates hormone depending on the isoenzyme and ring involved. (Book p901)

items.q: Match the following deiodinase distributions — 1) Type I 2) Type II 3) Type III … A) Liver/kidney B) CNS/thyroid/pituitary C) Placenta/hemangioma
items.exp: These are the site groups printed in the three-column table; type II is labeled most abundant by the source. (Book p901)

items.q: A very large hemangioma is associated with accelerated thyroid-hormone inactivation. Which enzyme is the best match?
items.exp: The type III column includes hemangioma and conversion of T4 to reverse T3, consistent with an inactivating pathway. (Book p901)

items.q: Match the following deiodinase functions — 1) Type I 2) Type II 3) Type III … A) Local T4 to T3 activation B) Reverse-T3 degradation C) T4 to reverse T3
items.exp: The table emphasizes rT3 clearance for type I, T3 generation for type II and rT3 formation for type III. (Book p901)

items.q: In the source's illness model, assess: I Reduced type-II activity is followed by type-III activation. II Type III is an activating T4-to-T3 enzyme.
items.exp: The schematic depicts D2 inhibition followed by D3 activation, including a skeletal-muscle note; D3 inactivates rather than activates thyroid hormone. (Book p901)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the deiodinase inhibitors listed?
items.exp: PTU, amiodarone, steroids and propranolol are listed; methimazole's principal action is intrathyroidal TPO inhibition rather than peripheral conversion blockade. (Book p901)

items.q: Besides PTU, amiodarone and propranolol, the listed drug class reducing peripheral conversion is ___.
items.exp: Steroids are the fourth entry in the deiodinase-inhibitor list. (Book p901)

items.q: The table gives free fractions of T3 and T4 as approximately ___ and ___ respectively.
items.exp: T3 has the greater free fraction in the source comparison; the decimal places matter. (Book p901)

items.q: Match the following T3/T4 properties — 1) T3 half-life 2) T4 half-life 3) Relative biological potency … A) About one day B) T3:T4 about 4:1 C) About one week
items.exp: The table lists one day versus one week. Its row labeled 'Pathway' with values 4 and 1 is interpreted as relative potency, not four separate synthesis pathways. (Book p901)

items.q: After several days of fasting during critical illness, a patient has low T3, high reverse T3, and initially normal T4 and TSH. Which pattern matches the source?
items.exp: The early sick-euthyroid/low-T3 stage is T3 down, rT3 up and T4/TSH initially normal in the diagram. (Book p901)

items.q: Assess thyroid testing in critical illness: I ICU admission excludes coexisting intrinsic thyroid disease. II Thyroid testing remains appropriate when there is a specific clinical suspicion.
items.exp: Non-thyroidal illness complicates interpretation; it does not prohibit testing for a genuine thyroid indication. (Book p901)

items.q: In the source's middle-stage schematic, TSH and T3 ___, whereas reverse T3 and T4 ___.
items.exp: That is the printed middle-stage pattern. The T4 rise is not a required universal trajectory; real non-thyroidal illness can have normal or low T4 depending on severity and context. (Book p901)

items.q: Match the following source illness stages — 1) Early 2) Middle 3) Late … A) All four hormone entries fall B) TSH/T3 low, rT3/T4 high in this diagram C) T3 low/rT3 high, T4 and TSH initially normal
items.exp: The three-stage chart ends in rapid catabolism with lower T4, TSH, rT3 and T3. It is a teaching schematic, not a mandatory sequence in every patient. (Book p901)

items.q: A critically ill patient's late-stage chart shows all measured thyroid-related hormones falling. Which explanation is printed at that stage?
items.exp: The final branch labels rapid catabolism with falls in T4, TSH, rT3 and T3; clinical interpretation must still consider medications and genuine thyroid disease. (Book p901)
